notes:
Group sa-02-a. Page budget: five pages (Maurya Empire, Seleucid-Mauryan war, Kalinga War, Bindusara, Shunga Empire) plus the Kalinga region page already opened for the Kalinga dossier.

START AND END. The page gives 'around c. 320 BCE' for the founding and 'ca. 322-319' for the victory over the Nandas; Cliopatria starts in -318; the Nanda dossier ends the Nandas in -322. The dossier starts in -322 (the first year of the page's range) so that no year is left without a state. The end is the infobox's 185 BCE; Cliopatria keeps a Maurya row to -171 and starts the Shunga in -170. The Shunga dossier (another part of sa-02) should start no later than -184 on the Gangetic core; this dossier leaves -184..-171 to it.

WHAT THE PAGES DO NOT SAY. (1) The date and places of the loss of the outer empire after Ashoka: the page says only that the empire 'lost many territories under Dasharatha' and 'slowly' afterwards. Cliopatria drops 71 percent of the area in one step (-225); the ledger records it at confidence 1 (loss to the Satavahanas for the Deccan, and 'nobody' for the Northwest, east and west, which no Cliopatria state holds afterwards). The Greco-Bactrian and Indo-Greek dossiers (me-05, Greek agents) should say who held Gandhara, Arachosia and the Punjab between 224 and 180 BCE. (2) Conquests in Malwa, Gujarat, Saurashtra, Bengal, Assam: no sentence on the page. (3) The extent of the Cliopatria shapes in the east is unverified.

DISAGREEMENTS. Brihadratha's death: 185 (infobox), 184 (timeline), 180 BCE (text). Seleucid cession: Maurya page 'certainly Gandhara, Parapamisadae, eastern Gedrosia, possibly Arachosia and Aria'; war page Aria, Arachosia, Gedrosia, Paropamisadae, and no Gandhara. Ashoka's accession 272/269/268. Bindusara's southern conquest: the Maurya page says he extended the empire to Karnataka; the Bindusara page gives Sen (no extension) and Daniélou (nominal control of the Cheras, Cholas and Satyaputras) against Taranatha. The southern limit follows the Maurya page (Karnataka) and Kulke and Rothermund (Kerala and Tamil Nadu not included); Andhra and Maharashtra are 'large parts' only, so they were left in the shape.

CORRECTIONS MADE. Tamil Nadu and Kerala removed from the Ashokan shapes (about 78,000 km2); Kalinga years (annexed -261 not -256); Odisha removed from the post-224 remnant; the shape ends -185 not -171; new first keyframe -322..-319.

COUNTERPARTS. 'macedonian-empire' for the Northwest and 'seleucid-empire' for the ceded satrapies are Cliopatria readings (the lands are Macedonian Empire cells until -292 in Cliopatria, though the Seleucid page says Seleucus ceded them). Their dossiers should carry the matching losses. 'kalinga' and 'satavahana-dynasty' are in this group. The Edict-13 neighbours (Cholas, Pandyas, Satiyaputras, Keralaputras, Tamraparni) are 'friendly' neighbours, not vassals, so no vassal events were written.

GAZETTEER. All names used exist (Magadha; Odisha, Tamil Nadu and Kerala as admin1; Cliopatria shapes); the Paropamisadae region has no gazetteer entry; after the repair it is spelled as nine Afghan admin-1 units (Kabul, Kapisa, Parwan, Panjshir, Wardak, Logar, Nangarhar, Laghman, Kunar) and Arachosia as four (Kandahar, Zabul, Uruzgan, Ghazni). A gazetteer region 'Paropamisadae' would replace the first union.

REPAIR (2026-10-19, after the adversarial review). (1) The Northwest was drawn wrongly: Cliopatria's -315 enlargement is mostly Baluchistan (852 of 1,561 cells), which both pages put in the cession of ca. 302 BCE ('the eastern parts of Gedrosia'; 'Gedrosia' in the war infobox). Baluchistan is now taken out of the 316 gain and the -315 keyframe (the Indus valley, Sindh and the southern Punjab, remains) and enters with the 302 cession. (2) The 302 cession region now holds what the pages name: Cliopatria's -301 enlargement (Gandhara, the Punjab, Kashmir), all of Pakistani Baluchistan, the Paropamisadae (nine Afghan provinces) and Arachosia (four; hedged: 'possibly' on the Maurya page, listed without a hedge on the war page, Kandahar inscription of 260 BCE). Aria (Herat) is left out because every page hedges it (Chandragupta page: 'rejected by contemporary scholarship'). (3) The -301, -291, -256 and -247 keyframes carry the Afghan and Baluchistan lands to -226; the -225 loss removes them. The 305-303 contest zone and the war zones were aligned with the gain regions. (4) Rulers Bindusara to Brihadratha cite the Maurya Empire page. DISAGREEMENTS KEPT: the Chandragupta page says the extent of the cession is unknown, that a 'modest interpretation limits the extension to the western Indus Valley' with the Punjab, the eastern Paropamisadae and the Gedrosian coast, and that Tarn and Coningham and Young question Kabul-Kandahar; the Maurya page says 'certainly' for the Paropamisadae. The dossier follows the Maurya page and the war page (both list it) and flags this. The war page says the Mauryas annexed the governors' areas 'all the way to the banks of the Indus', and also that Seleucus ceded the Punjab: the Punjab is split between the 316 gain (south, Cliopatria's -315 cells) and the 302 cession (the rest). MISMATCH WITH macedonian-empire (another batch, not edited): its ledger has a loss to maurya-empire at -317 of 'Gandhara and the Punjab'; this dossier gains the Indus valley (Sindh, southern Punjab) at -316 and Gandhara only at -302 from seleucid-empire. The two should be reconciled by the Macedonian reviewer: either Gandhara moves to this dossier's 316 gain (the Maurya page lists it in the 302 cession, the Chandragupta page puts the Punjab campaign c. 317 and Daniélou has Philip's Gandhara taken by Chandragupta) or the Macedonian loss is shortened to the Indus valley. THIN ITEMS READ (four extra pages: 10 pages in all against the budget of 5): the Edicts of Ashoka, Chandragupta Maurya, Dasharatha Maurya and Satavahana dynasty pages date none of the southern gain, the Deccan loss or the post-Ashokan losses; the ledger events stay at confidence 1 with the new quotes in their notes. New lead: the Chandragupta page puts Gujarat and Malwa under Chandragupta, while Cliopatria adds Gujarat only in -291; a gap-filler can decide whether the -301 keyframe should hold them. The eastern extent (Bengal, Assam) is still unverified: no page opened mentions either.
